title: What Does a Carpet Warranty Actually Cover?
meta: A carpet warranty covers fiber wear, texture loss and listed stains, not traffic lanes or pet damage. What Seattle homeowners can really claim. Wills Flooring.
keywords: what does a carpet warranty cover, carpet warranty exclusions, carpet wear warranty explained, carpet stain warranty claim, carpet installation Seattle WA

blocks.lead: A carpet warranty covers three narrow things: the fiber wearing away by more than a stated percentage, the texture matting beyond a rated level, and specific food and beverage stains that will not clean out. It does not cover crushing in traffic lanes, pet urine, fading, seams or anything the maker can blame on the pad or the cleaning schedule.
blocks.detail: Add the installer's workmanship warranty, which is a separate document, and you have the whole picture. Wills Flooring backs every carpet install with a 1-year workmanship warranty on top of the manufacturer's coverage.

blocks.html: Seattle buyers read the sample tag in a Ballard living room, see a 20-year or lifetime warranty, and reasonably assume the carpet is guaranteed for 20 years. Then the hallway in a Queen Anne rental looks flat after four years and the claim is denied. The tag was not lying. It was describing something much more specific than most people think. This post walks through each warranty type, what voids it, and how a real claim goes.

blocks.text: The four warranties on a carpet label

items.title: Abrasive wear
items.text: The fiber must lose more than a set percentage of its pile weight, usually 10 percent, in any one area. That means fiber physically gone, measured in a lab. Flattened, dull or discolored pile is not wear under this definition, and it is the warranty most people think they have.

items.title: Texture retention
items.text: The maker rates the carpet on a matting and crushing scale after a test walk. The claim succeeds if your carpet drops below that rating. In practice it is judged from photos and a site visit, and traffic lanes are almost always argued to be soiling or improper cleaning instead.

items.title: Stain and soil
items.text: Coverage is for a listed set of household food and drink stains that resist proper cleaning. Typical exclusions: pet urine, vomit, bleach, hair dye, mustard, hot beverages and anything with strong dye. Soil warranties cover dry dirt attaching to the fiber, not the gray look of a lane.

items.title: Installation workmanship
items.text: This is the installer's, not the mill's. It covers seams opening, ripples from a loose stretch, and transitions coming up. At Wills Flooring that is a 1-year warranty, and it is the one that actually gets used, because most visible first-year problems are installation, not fiber.

blocks.text: What the fine print excludes, in almost every brand

head: Problem you see
Covered?
Why not
rows: Traffic lane in the hall looks darker and flatter
Classified as soiling and crushing from use. Only a measured texture drop below the rating counts.
Dog urine spot that will not come out
Pet stains are excluded from nearly all stain warranties unless you bought a specific pet-labeled product, and even those require prompt cleaning.
Fading by a south window in West Seattle
Sunlight and ozone fading are excluded. Solution-dyed fibers resist it better, but it is not a warranty item.
Carpet on stairs wearing at the nose
Most wear warranties exclude stairs entirely or cut the coverage period in half.
Seam showing or ripples after a year
That is workmanship. The mill will point you to whoever installed it, which is why the installer's warranty matters.
Considered a characteristic of cut-pile carpet, not a defect.
blocks.note: Every brand words these differently. Read the actual warranty PDF for the product you are buying, not the sample tag.

blocks.text: The conditions that quietly void coverage

items.html: The wrong pad. Nearly every warranty specifies a minimum pad density and a maximum thickness. A thick, soft pad from a big-box bundle can void the texture warranty on day one. We match the pad to the mill spec and note it on your quote. More on that in our carpet padding explainer.

No professional cleaning receipts. Most warranties require hot-water extraction by a certified cleaner every 12 to 24 months, with proof. No receipts, no claim. Put a reminder in your calendar the day the carpet goes in.
The wrong cleaning method. Some brands exclude damage from rental machines or from cleaners that are not on their approved list. Check before you rent.
Installed in an excluded room. Stairs, bathrooms, outdoor and commercial uses are commonly excluded. A Capitol Hill condo used as a short-term rental can be treated as commercial.
Not registering or losing the invoice. Some warranties transfer only to the original buyer and require the dated invoice showing the product name and style number. Keep ours with the house papers.

blocks.text: How a claim actually plays out

items.d: Step 1: call the installer, not the mill
items.text: Most problems in year one are stretch, seams or transitions, and those are on us. We come out, look, and fix workmanship issues under the 1-year warranty at no charge.

items.d: Step 2: document before you clean again
items.text: Photos in daylight, the invoice, the style number from the back of a leftover piece, and your cleaning receipts. Note where the problem is and when you first saw it.

The manufacturer sends an independent inspector who measures pile height, takes a sample and checks the pad. In Seattle this can take a few weeks to schedule. The report goes to the mill, not to you, so ask for a copy.

If approved, the usual remedy is replacement carpet of comparable value, prorated by age, and sometimes a labor allowance. Full refunds are rare. It is worth knowing this before you decide whether to file.

blocks.text: Mistakes that turn a good carpet into a denied claim

a.title: Do this
items: Buy the pad the mill specifies, not the thickest one on the shelf
Book hot-water extraction every 12 to 18 months and keep the receipt
Blot spills right away, water first, then the maker's cleaner
Keep the invoice, style number and a leftover scrap
Report seams and ripples to your installer in the first year

b.title: Avoid this
items: Assuming a lifetime tag means the carpet will look new for life
Letting pet accidents sit overnight, then claiming a stain defect
Using a rental machine with the wrong chemistry on a treated fiber
Putting bedroom-grade carpet on a Wallingford staircase and expecting stair coverage
Buying online with no installer, so nobody owns the workmanship

blocks.title: A Seattle note on condos and rentals:
blocks.text: Many Capitol Hill and Belltown buildings require carpet in bedrooms for sound. If you rent the unit out, some manufacturers reclassify the use as commercial and shorten residential coverage. Ask us to check the brand's wording before you buy for a rental.
What to ask before you sign for carpet

items: Which warranties apply to this exact style: wear, texture, stain, soil, and for how many years each.
Whether stairs are covered, and for how long.
Which pad density and thickness the mill requires, and whether the quote uses it.
How often professional cleaning is required and what counts as proof.
Whether the warranty transfers if you sell the house.
What the installer's workmanship warranty covers and for how long. Ours is 1 year, in writing.
Who you call first when something goes wrong. The answer should be a local phone number, ours is (425) 350-4435.

faq.q: Does a carpet wear warranty cover matting and crushing?
faq.a: Not the wear warranty. Wear means fiber physically lost, usually more than 10 percent of pile weight in an area. Matting and crushing fall under a separate texture retention warranty, which is judged against the carpet's rated level. Traffic-lane flattening is usually argued to be soiling, so it is the hardest claim to win.

faq.q: Are pet stains covered by carpet stain warranties?
faq.a: Almost never under a standard stain warranty. Pet urine, feces and vomit are listed exclusions for most brands. Some pet-specific carpet lines do cover them, but they require prompt cleaning and the specified pad. If you have dogs or cats in Seattle, buy a product that names pets in its warranty.

faq.q: Do I really need professional cleaning to keep a carpet warranty?
faq.a: Yes for most brands. The typical requirement is hot-water extraction by a professional every 12 to 24 months, with dated receipts kept as proof. Skipping it is one of the most common reasons a claim is denied, regardless of what the fiber actually did.

faq.q: Is carpet on stairs covered by the warranty?
faq.a: Usually not, or only for a shorter period. Stairs concentrate wear on the nose of each tread, so most mills exclude them or halve the coverage. If a Seattle staircase is a big part of your project, choose a dense nylon and treat stair wear as a maintenance item rather than a warranty one.

faq.q: What does the installer's workmanship warranty cover?
faq.a: Problems from the installation itself: seams peaking or opening, ripples from a loose stretch, transitions coming up, and tack strip issues. Wills Flooring covers these for 1 year at no charge. It is separate from the manufacturer's fiber warranties and is the one most likely to be used.

faq.q: What do I actually get if a carpet warranty claim is approved?
faq.a: Usually replacement carpet of comparable quality, prorated by how many years you have had it, and sometimes a contribution toward labor. Cash refunds are rare. Reading the remedy section before buying tells you how much the long warranty number is really worth.
